Dynamic Chunking backpropagates gradients through discrete boundary decisions without explicit boundary labels by using a **smoothing module** that transforms the discrete upsampling operation into a continuous one. This module applies an **exponential moving average (EMA)** defined as $\bar{z}_t = P_t \hat{z}_t + (1 - P_t)\bar{z}_{t-1}$, where $P_t$ represents the confidence score of the boundary [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, Sec 2.2 Dynamic Chunking (DC), p. 7].

This mechanism enables **differentiable boundary learning** by creating smooth interpolations between chunks, which allows for effective backpropagation through chunk boundaries during training without requiring stochastic exploration-based approaches [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, Sec 2.2 Dynamic Chunking (DC), p. 7]. Additionally, the smoothing module contributes to **training stability** by preventing the model from overfitting to suboptimal chunking patterns early in training [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, Sec 2.2 Dynamic Chunking (DC), p. 7]. The paper notes that this approach avoids the high-variance gradients and training instability associated with stochastic exploration methods like those used in the Dynamic Pooling Transformer [Dynamic Chunking for End-to-End Hierarchical Sequence Modeling, Sec References, p. 33].
